chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Idris, from someone whose name he mentioned, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, who raised it (to the Prophet), saying:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: O Ali! Whoever visits me during my life or after my death, or visits you during your life or after your death, or visits your two sons during their lives or after their death, I guarantee for him on the Day of Resurrection that I will deliver him from its terrors and hardships until I place him with me in my rank.

key_terms.أَهْوَالِهَا: The terrors and fears of the Day of Judgment
key_terms.ابْنَيْكَ: Your two sons (referring to Imam Hasan and Imam al-Husayn)
key_terms.دَرَجَتِي: My rank/position (referring to the Prophet's spiritual station)
key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation (Ziyarah), specifically referring to visiting the graves or shrines of the Prophet and Imams
key_terms.شَدَائِدِهَا: The hardships and difficulties of the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet and the Imams according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the theological principle of *Ziyarah* as a means of intercession and spiritual elevation, linking the visitor directly to the Ahl al-Bayt. It underscores the Shia belief that visiting the Prophet and the Imams, whether in life or after death, secures deliverance from the *Ahwal* (terrors) of the Hereafter and grants entry into the Prophet's specific station (*Darajah*).
